# Weak and doubled roots

## Introduction

The letters
alif/hamzah
([أ]{.ar}),
[و]{.ar},
and
[ي]{.ar}
are considered weak letters.
When any of these letters are part of the root of a verb,
then that verb is called a _weak verb_.
When weak verbs are conjugated for different doers,
then the weak letters can modify the appearance of the conjugated verb
in different ways.

Of the weak letters, hamzah is the strongest (in pronunciation, though it is weak in writing).
And it will usually (though not always) retain its pronunciation when a verb with hamzah in its root is conjugated.
So we will treat it separately at the end.

## The weak middle-letter verb

### [و]{.ar} as the weak middle-letter

Consider the root
[قول]{.ar} with the meaning [to say]{.trans}.

When we form the [mADI]{.trn2} verb from roots with [و]{.ar} as the middle root letter,
we usually assume a [fatHah]{.trn2} on the middle root letter.

Therefore, we would expect the verb for the doer [he]{.trans}
to be
[قَوَلَ]{.ar}
[qawala]{.trn}.^[[[شرح ألفية ابن مالك للعثيمين]{.ar} 31/7](https://shamela.ws/book/36954/310)]
Instead, however,
the sequence [قَوَ]{.ar} [qawa]{.trn} is modified to [قَا]{.ar} [qA]{.trn},
and we will actually say:

(@) [قَالَ]{.ar}  
    [qAla]{.trn}  
    [He said]{.trans}

Similarly, when we conjugate for the doer
[she]{.trans},
we would expect to say
[قَوَلَتْ]{.ar}
[qawalat]{.trn},
but we actually say:

(@) [قَالَتْ]{.ar}
    [qAlat]{.trn}  
    [She said]{.trans}

Continuing on, when we conjugate for the doer [I]{.trans},
we would expect to say
[قَوَلْتُ]{.ar}
[qawaltu]{.trn}.
In this case, we don't convert
[قَوَ]{.ar} [qawa]{.trn} to [قَا]{.ar} [qA]{.trn}
because
then we would end up with
[قَالْتُ]{.ar}
[qAltu]{.trn}.
But a long vowel followed by a [sukUn]{.trn2} is disallowed phonologically
in Arabic
(except when pausing at the end of an utterance).
So we cannot say ✗\ [قَالْتُ]{.ar} [qAltu]{.trn}.

Instead, we eliminiate the middle letter altogether,
and place a [Dammah]{.trn2} on the [ق]{.ar} because it is the closest vowel to the original root letter [و]{.ar}.
So we say:

(@) [قُلْتُ]{.ar}  
    [qultu]{.trn}  
    [I said]{.trans}  

Similarly we will say

(@) [قُلْتَ]{.ar}  
    [qulta]{.trn}  
    [You~sing.m.~ said]{.trans}  

(@) [قُلْتِ]{.ar}  
    [qulti]{.trn}  
    [You~sing.f.~ said]{.trans}  

Moving on to the duals,
for strong verbs we simply add an alif to
[ذَهَبَ]{.ar}
[he went]{.trans}
to get
[ذَهَبَا]{.ar}
[they~du.m.~ went]{.trans}.
And from
[ذَهَبَتْ]{.ar}
[she went]{.trans}
we get
[ذَهَبَتَا]{.ar}
[they~du.f.~ went]{.trans}.

We will do the same thing to
[قَالَ]{.ar}
and
[قَالَتْ]{.ar}
respectively.
So we get:

(@) [قَالَا]{.ar}  
    [qAlA]{.trn}  
    [They~du.m.~ said]{.trans}

(@) [قَالَتَا]{.ar}  
    [qAlatA]{.trn}  
    [They~du.f.~ said]{.trans}

For [you~du.~ said]{.trans},
we use
[قُلْتُ]{.ar}
[I said]{.trans}
as our starting point and replace the doer pronoun [تُ]{.ar}
[I]{.trans}
with
[تُمَا]{.ar}
[you~du.~]{.trans}.
So we say

(@) [قُلْتُمَا]{.ar}  
    [qultumA]{.trn}  
    [You~du.~ said]{.trans}  

Now let's move on to the plurals.
For strong verbs we modify
[ذَهَبَ]{.ar}
[he went]{.trans}
by adding the doer pronoun [ـُوا]{.ar} [they~pl.m.~]{.trans}
and we get
[ذَهَبُوا]{.ar}
[they~pl.m.~ went]{.trans}.
We will do the same thing to [قَالَ]{.ar}
[he said]{.trans}
to get:

(@) [قَالُوا]{.ar}  
    [qAlU]{.trn}  
    [They~pl.m.~ said]{.trans}  

For [they~pl.f.~]{.ar},
there is a [sukUn]{.trn2} on the final root letter
(e.g. [ذَهَبْنَ]{.ar} [they~pl.f~ went]{.trans}).
So now we use the pattern
[قُلْتُ]{.ar} I said]{.ar},
and replace the doer pronoun [تُ]{.ar} [I]{.trans}
with [نَ]{.ar} [they~pl.f.~]{.trans}.
So we will say:

(@) [قُلْنَ]{.ar}  
    [qulna]{.trn}  
    [They~pl.f.~ said]{.trans}  

Similarly, for [you~pl.m~]{.trans}
we will say:

(@) [قُلْتُمْ]{.ar}  
    [qultum]{.trn}  
    [You~pl.m.~ said]{.trans}  

and
for [you~pl.f~]{.trans}
we will say:

(@) [قُلْتُنَّ]{.ar}  
    [qultunna]{.trn}  
    [You~pl.f.~ said]{.trans}  

Lastly, for [we]{.trans},
we will do the same thing and say:

(@) [قُلْنَا]{.ar}
    [qulnA]{.trn}  
    [We said]{.trans}  

Here is the complete verb conjugation table:

|Doer pronoun | Conjugation |
|:-----|:---|
|[He said]{.trans} | [قَالَ]{.ar} |
|[She said]{.trans} | [قَالَتْ]{.ar} |
|[You~sing.m.~ said]{.trans} | [قُلْتَ]{.ar} |
|[You~sing.f.~ said]{.trans} | [قُلْتِ]{.ar} |
|[I said]{.trans} | [قُلْتُ]{.ar} |
|[They~du.m.~ said]{.trans} | [قَالَا]{.ar} |
|[They~du.f.~ said]{.trans} | [قَالَتَا]{.ar} |
|[You~du.~ said]{.trans} | [قُلْتُمَا]{.ar} |
|[They~pl.m.~ said]{.trans} | [قَالُوا]{.ar} |
|[They~pl.f.~ said]{.trans} | [قُلْنَ]{.ar} |
|[You~pl.m.~ said]{.trans} | [قُلْتُمْ]{.ar} |
|[You~pl.f.~ said]{.trans} | [قُلْتُنَّ]{.ar} |
|[We said]{.trans} | [قُلْنَا]{.ar} |

### [#kasrah]{.trn2} on the middle [و]{.ar} letter

Most verbs that have [و]{.ar} as the middle root letter behave as above,
with an original [fatHah]{.trn2} on the [و]{.ar} becoming an alif:

(@) [قَوَلَ]{.ar} → [قَالَ]{.ar}  
    [qawala]{.trn} → [qAla]{.trn}  
    [He said]{.trans}  

And when the [و]{.ar} is eliminated, it is replaced with a [Dammah]{.trn2} on the first root letter:

(@) [قَوَلْتُ]{.ar} → [قُلْتُ]{.ar}  
    [qawaltu]{.trn} → [qultu]{.trn}  
    [I said]{.trans}  

A few verbs, however, take a [kasrah]{.trn2} on the middle [و]{.ar}.
For example, the root [خوف]{.ar} [to fear]{.trans}.
In this case, the [و]{.ar} still becomes an alif:

(@) [خَوِفَ]{.ar} → [خَافَ]{.ar}  
    [xawifa]{.trn} → [xAfa]{.trn}  
    [He feared]{.trans}  

But when the [و]{.ar} is eliminated, it is replaced with a [kasrah]{.trn2} on the first root letter:

(@) [خَوِفْتُ]{.ar} → [خِفْتُ]{.ar}  
    [xawiftu]{.trn} → [xiftu]{.trn}  
    [He feared]{.trans}  

Here is the complete conjugation table:

|Doer pronoun | Conjugation |
|:-----|:---|
|[He feared]{.trans} | [خَافَ]{.ar} |
|[She feared]{.trans} | [خَافَتْ]{.ar} |
|[You~sing.m.~ feared]{.trans} | [خِفْتَ]{.ar} |
|[You~sing.f.~ feared]{.trans} | [خِفْتِ]{.ar} |
|[I feared]{.trans} | [خِفْتُ]{.ar} |
|[They~du.m.~ feared]{.trans} | [خَافَا]{.ar} |
|[They~du.f.~ feared]{.trans} | [خَافَتَا]{.ar} |
|[You~du.~ feared]{.trans} | [خِفْتُمَا]{.ar} |
|[They~pl.m.~ feared]{.trans} | [خَافُوا]{.ar} |
|[They~pl.f.~ feared]{.trans} | [خِفْنَ]{.ar} |
|[You~pl.m.~ feared]{.trans} | [خِفْتُمْ]{.ar} |
|[You~pl.f.~ feared]{.trans} | [خِفْتُنَّ]{.ar} |
|[We feared]{.trans} | [خِفْنَا]{.ar} |

The verb [نَامَ]{.ar} [to sleep]{.trans} from the root [نوم]{.ar} behaves similarly.

### [ي]{.ar} as the weak middle-letter

When [ي]{.ar} is the 
weak middle-letter,
as in the verb root [بيع]{.ar} [to sell]{.trans},
then we follow pretty much the same procedure as for [قَالَ]{.ar}.
So:

(@) [بَيَعَ]{.ar} → [بَاعَ]{.ar}  
    [bayaea]{.trn} → [bAea]{.trn}  
    [He sold]{.trans}  

But when the [ي]{.ar} is eliminated, it is replaced with a [kasrah]{.trn2} on the first root letter,
because the [kasrah]{.trn2} is the closer vowel to [ي]{.ar}.

(@) [بَيَعْتُ]{.ar} → [بِعْتُ]{.ar}  
    [bayaetu]{.trn} → [bietu]{.trn}  
    [I sold]{.trans}  


Here is the complete verb conjugation table:

|Doer pronoun | Conjugation |
|:-----|:---|
|[He sold]{.trans} | [بَاعَ]{.ar} |
|[She sold]{.trans} | [بَاعَتْ]{.ar} |
|[You~sing.m.~ sold]{.trans} | [بِعْتَ]{.ar} |
|[You~sing.f.~ sold]{.trans} | [بِعْتِ]{.ar} |
|[I sold]{.trans} | [بِعْتُ]{.ar} |
|[They~du.m.~ sold]{.trans} | [بَاعَا]{.ar} |
|[They~du.f.~ sold]{.trans} | [بَاعَتَا]{.ar} |
|[You~du.~ sold]{.trans} | [بِعْتُمَا]{.ar} |
|[They~pl.m.~ sold]{.trans} | [بَاعُوا]{.ar} |
|[They~pl.f.~ sold]{.trans} | [بِعْنَ]{.ar} |
|[You~pl.m.~ sold]{.trans} | [بِعْتُمْ]{.ar} |
|[You~pl.f.~ sold]{.trans} | [بِعْتُنَّ]{.ar} |
|[We sold]{.trans} | [بِعْنَا]{.ar} |


## The weak final-letter verb

### [و]{.ar} as the weak final-letter

Consider the verb root [دعو]{.ar} [to call]{.trans}.

When we form the [mADI]{.trn2} verb from roots with [و]{.ar} as the middle root letter,
we usually assume a [fatHah]{.trn2} on the middle root letter.

Therefore, we would expect the verb for the doer [he]{.trans}
to be
[دَعَوَ]{.ar}
[daeawa]{.trn}.
Instead, however,
the sequence [عَوَ]{.ar} [eawa]{.trn} is modified to [عَا]{.ar} [eA]{.trn},
and we will actually say:

(@) [دَعَا]{.ar}  
    [daeA]{.trn}  
    [He called]{.trans}


Similarly, when we conjugate for the doer
[she]{.trans},
we would expect to say
[دَعَوَتْ]{.ar}
[daeawat]{.trn},
but we actually say:

(@) [دَعَتْ]{.ar}
    [daeat]{.trn}  
    [She called]{.trans}

Continuing on, there is no modification of the root [و]{.ar} when we conjugate for the doer [I]{.trans}.

(@) [دَعَوْتُ]{.ar}  
    [daeawtu]{.trn}  
    [I called]{.trans}  

Similarly we will say:

(@) [دَعَوْتَ]{.ar}  
    [daeawta]{.trn}  
    [You~sing.m.~ called]{.trans}  

(@) [دَعَوْتِ]{.ar}  
    [daeawti]{.trn}  
    [You~sing.f.~ called]{.trans}  

Moving on to the duals,
we add back the [و]{.ar} to the verb when we add on the alif for the [they~du.m.~]{.trans}.
So we get:

(@) [دَعَوَا]{.ar}  
    [daeawA]{.trn}  
    [They~du.m.~ called]{.trans}

For
[they~du.m.~]{.trans},
we simply add an alif to [دَعَتْ]{.ar} [she called]{.trans},
and we get:

(@) [دَعَتَا]{.ar}  
    [daeatA]{.trn}  
    [They~du.f.~ called]{.trans}

For [you~du.~ called]{.trans},
there is again no modification of the root [و]{.ar}.
So we say:

(@) [دَعَوْتُمَا]{.ar}  
    [daeawtumA]{.trn}  
    [You~du.~ called]{.trans}  

Now let's move on to the plurals.
For [they~pl.m.~]{.trans},
we need to add a [ـُوا]{.ar},
but because there is already a [و]{.ar} in the root,
we don't add another one.
Instead we put a [sukUn]{.trn2} on it
to get:

(@) [دَعَوْا]{.ar}  
    [daeaw]{.trn}  
    [They~pl.m.~ called]{.trans}  

When 
[دَعَوْا]{.ar}
is to be connected to a following connecting-hamzah,
then we will put a [Dammah]{.trn2} on the [و]{.ar}.
For example:

(@) [دَعَوُا ٱلرَّجُلَ]{.ar}  
    [daeawu -rrajula]{.trn}  
    [They~pl.m.~ called the man.]{.trans}  

For [they~pl.f.~]{.ar},
there is again no modification of the root [و]{.ar}.
So we say:

(@) [دَعَوْنَ]{.ar}  
    [daeawna]{.trn}  
    [They~pl.f.~ called]{.trans}  

Similarly, for [you~pl.m~]{.trans}
we will say:

(@) [دَعَوْتُمْ]{.ar}  
    [daeawtum]{.trn}  
    [You~pl.m.~ called]{.trans}  

and
for [you~pl.f~]{.trans}
we will say:

(@) [دَعَوْتُنَّ]{.ar}  
    [daeawtunna]{.trn}  
    [You~pl.f.~ called]{.trans}  

Lastly, for [we]{.trans},
we will do the same thing and say:

(@) [دَعَوْنَا]{.ar}
    [daeawnA]{.trn}  
    [We called]{.trans}  

Here is the complete verb conjugation table:

|Doer pronoun | Conjugation |
|:-----|:---|
|[He said]{.trans} | [دَعَا]{.ar} |
|[She said]{.trans} | [دَعَتْ]{.ar} |
|[You~sing.m.~ said]{.trans} | [دَعَوْتَ]{.ar} |
|[You~sing.f.~ said]{.trans} | [دَعَوْتِ]{.ar} |
|[I said]{.trans} | [دَعَوْتُ]{.ar} |
|[They~du.m.~ said]{.trans} | [دَعَوَا]{.ar} |
|[They~du.f.~ said]{.trans} | [دَعَتَا]{.ar} |
|[You~du.~ said]{.trans} | [دَعَوْتُمَا]{.ar} |
|[They~pl.m.~ said]{.trans} | [دَعَوْا]{.ar} |
|[They~pl.f.~ said]{.trans} | [دَعَوْنَ]{.ar} |
|[You~pl.m.~ said]{.trans} | [دَعَوْتُمْ]{.ar} |
|[You~pl.f.~ said]{.trans} | [دَعَوْتُنَّ]{.ar} |
|[We said]{.trans} | [دَعَوْنَا]{.ar} |

## The doubled verb


## [كَانَ]{.ar}
